verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a complex, indirect relationship between estrone and L-lactate dehydrogenase C chain, mediated through a monoclonal antibody (mAb) 2E2 and 2'-hydroxymatteucinol. Estrone, through its interaction with mAb 2E2, is linked to 2'-hydroxymatteucinol, which in turn targets L-lactate dehydrogenase C chain. This pathway implies that estrone may influence the activity of L-lactate dehydrogenase C chain via a non-enzymatic mechanism, possibly through the modulation of a signaling molecule or the activation of a cellular response. The presence of a monoclonal antibody as a bridge highlights the potential role of immune-mediated interactions in this relationship, suggesting a possible involvement of the immune system in the regulation of L-lactate dehydrogenase C chain activity. The evidence supports a mechanism where estrone indirectly affects the enzyme through a series of molecular interactions, though the exact nature of these interactions remains to be fully elucidated.
